lesson_title: Push the Wall, the Wall Pushes Back
hook_text: Every time you take a step, the ground pushes you forward. Here is the rule behind it.
clip_script: A force is a push, a pull or a twist. It can start something moving, stop it, speed it up, slow it down, turn it or squash it. We measure forces in newtons, and a small apple in your hand pushes down with about one newton. Now the big rule. Forces always come in pairs. Push a wall, and the wall pushes back on you just as hard. Stand on roller skates and push, and you roll away backwards. That push-back is how everything moves. Your foot pushes the ground backwards; the ground pushes you forwards. On ice your foot slips, the ground cannot push back, and you go nowhere. A swimmer pushes water back and glides forward. A rocket blasts gas down and the gas shoves it up, even in empty space. Equal, opposite, and on different objects, so they never cancel.
visual_style: A skater pushing off a wall; slow-motion foot pushing on a running track with arrows; a swimmer's stroke; a rocket launch with paired arrows.
pacing: Quick definition, a punchy rule, then a fast montage of examples.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the force pair in every move you make.
